concurrency.rule: If available Codex concurrency is lower than 32, every assignment is still created and queued. When a task finishes, the next queued task starts immediately.
startOrder: SRC01-SRC04 and every PF lane holding families start together — the conveyor and the builders are not sequential
VF lanes start on the first PF checkpoint, not on a completed assignment
FIX lanes start on the first FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED verdict
an empty PF lane starts the moment a source lane releases a family into it
concurrency.idleRule: A lane is idle only when no executable work exists for its kind. An empty PF lane at dispatch is idle because the source queue is empty for it, and the source lanes are the work that ends that.

assignments.preflightMustReturn: PACKET_BUILD_ENVIRONMENT_READY with every registered applicable check passing
rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.
claimRule: Assert only these 2 exact families before reading or writing family content:
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'nc_145_8a_youthful-set'`
`node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert PF01 'ar-act346-set'`
A non-zero exit is a full stop for that family: report `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM` naming the exact refusal, and read none of its artifacts.
Do not release a claim in a worker return. Captain releases it centrally after integrating the bounded return.
assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Build 2 packet families to the builder contract, one at a time, checkpointing as you go. A family that stops does not stop the lane.

rowStopContract.everyFamilyGetsExactlyOneRow: COMPLETED or STOPPED, one row per assigned family, no family missing and none twice. A lane that returns fewer rows than it was assigned families has lost work silently.

rowStopContract.theLaneCompletesNormally: A lane with blocked families still completes. Blocked rows are the finding, not a failure of the lane.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

proofObligations: ROUTE IDENTITY: the packet is built for the route the record names
SOURCE IDENTITY: every source binds by exact SHA-256, recomputed from the bytes
COMPONENT SET: every component the route names is rendered and present
KNOWN PREFILLS: every known required fact is written and visible on the page it belongs to
REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING: every declared item is named in participant-instructions.md, checked against the file
ROUTE OPTIONS: every route-determined election is selected
REPEATING ROWS: no row carries written cells beside required cells left blank
PROTECTED FIELDS: no signature, signature date, certificate of mailing, court-only or prosecutor-only field carries ink
ARTIFACTS: canonical and boundary bytes hash to what the record names
PAGE ORDER: the rendered page order matches the packet manifest
CLIPPING AND OVERLAP: no ink outside a measured write box
FILING DESTINATION: the instructions name the court or agency the route names
FEE AND WAIVER: the fee and any waiver route are stated
SERVICE: who must be served, and how
SELF-HELP STOP: the packet states where self-help ends

claimRule: Assert each exact source obligation before reading evidence: `node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert DISC01 <itemId>`
The committed assignment contains exactly 0 itemIds; iterate those values only. A familyId is metadata and is not a source claim key.
A non-zero exit stops that row only: record `BLOCKED_BEFORE_CLAIM`, read none of its evidence, and continue with unrelated obligations.

assignments.theDiffIsTheReturn: Commit locally. Leave the final diff for the Codex Cloud interface. There is no PUSHED line in a cloud return.
assignments.mission: Turn a descriptive label into a document identity: exact form number, official publisher, revision and the official URL it is published at. Resolve against committed inventories; never guess a form number. No obligation of this class is queued for this host group at dispatch; the lane starts the moment one arrives.

sourceRelationshipRegistry.readItBeforeYouFetchAnything: Look your obligation up by jurisdiction and canonical artifact id. Its sourceState tells you whether there is anything to fetch at all.

statesThatAreNotAFetch.BUNDLE_COMPONENT: 0 — the document is a page inside a public bundle whose address is already recorded. Record the component locator and alias. Acquire the BUNDLE once, never the page.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.EMBEDDED_SECTION: 0 — the document is a section inside another form. There is no separate binary to request from anyone.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.STALE_OR_VARIANT_ID: 0 — the identity is missing its current suffix or its filing-mode variant. Normalize the identity first; the form is public.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.SOURCE_SCOPE_AND_VERSION_AMBIGUITY: 0 — statewide versus local scope is unsettled. Settle the scope before any inquiry.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.FAMILY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: 1 — several held artifacts match this identity. Which one the route requires is the question; do not pick one.
statesThatAreNotAFetch.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: 7 — the corpus already HOLDS matching bytes. The open question is whether the publisher still issues that edition. This is not a missing source and it is not an acquisition.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

First the part that passes, so the failure is not overstated: the field map carries 57 refusals dispositioned REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING and I found all 57 of their effectiveLabel strings verbatim in participant-instructions.md, and both of the controlling manifest's obtain_document items - supporting evidence of trafficking, and the certified ALEA criminal record - are disclosed as numbered steps 1 and 2 of 'Do these before you file'. WHAT FAILS: the official CR-65 prints, in the delivered bytes, three elections it marks mandatory, and the packet neither makes them nor tells the participant to. (1) Packet page 6, under the printed heading 'I swear or affirm, under the penalty of perjury:', item '(3) (Select one of the following):' offers '[ ] that I have not previously applied for an expungement in this or any other jurisdiction.' and '[ ] that I have previously filed for an expungement.' In all four delivered fixtures BOTH boxes are blank. I confirmed this at appearance level by rendering delivered page 6 at 130 dpi and reading it. (2) Packet page 5 prints 'Attached to this Petition are: (Petition must include either item 1 or item 2; All Petitions must include item 3.)' over three boxes - certified record of arrest, certified record of disposition, and certified official criminal record from ALEA. All three are blank in all four fixtures, so neither the either-1-or-2 requirement nor the always-required item 3 is elected. NOW THE DISCLOSURE: I grepped both instruction files for 'select one', 'previously applied', 'previously filed', 'pro se', 'granted', 'denied', 'penalty of perjury', 'swear' and 'attach'. The only hit in either file is the closing line of filing-instructions.md, 'Do not sign or date the petition until every required blank and every attachment is complete' - which names no election and no attachment. Neither file names item (3), neither names the attachment boxes, and neither names the 'was [ ] granted [ ] denied' pair or the '[ ] pro se (Not represented by an attorney)' box, all of which are also blank on page 6. THE MECHANISM THAT KEEPS THE COUNTERS GREEN: the field map holds 50 selection-control refusals and 46 of them carry the identical boilerplate reason, 'A genuine participant election not determined by this route. This petition elects one statutory ground only.' That sentence is factually untrue of the page-5 attachment boxes, of the page-6 sworn select-one, of granted/denied and of pro se - none of them is a statutory ground. Worse, all 50 carry an effectiveLabel that is only the raw AcroForm field name ('Participant choice: Check Box2.0 (selection)'), so the record never states what any of these blanks says on the paper, and I confirmed that 0 of the 50 labels appears anywhere in participant-instructions.md. Every one of the 50 is recorded with requiredBeforeFiling false, which drops the mandatory ones out of the required-before-filing set entirely and is why nothing downstream can see them. A participant who follows this guide files a sworn CR-65 whose perjury clause has an unelected item (3) and whose attachment certification is unelected.

All 66 items appear in the file, so a presence test passes. Reading them defeats it. ACIC-PETITION-DRUG-COURT-POST:Sex carries effectiveLabel 'Race', so the instructions print two consecutive rows both named 'Race' for that document, no row named 'Sex', and the sentence 'supply Race from the court, ACIC, program-completion, or case record' against the Sex field. The registry track names two selfHelpStopConditions: 'The county attorney opposes the application.' and 'A disputed intervening conviction inside the two-year window.' The second reaches the participant: 'Check both against your own court record before you sign... If either is not true of your case, this is the wrong packet, and you should stop and talk to a lawyer.' The first reaches nobody. Neither delivered document has a stop-and-get-help section, and the only sentence touching opposition is filing-instructions.md 'After filing': 'The county attorney has an opportunity to respond.' A self-represented filer is told a response may come and is never told that opposition is where this packet's help ends. Sibling Illinois families in this same cohort carry an explicit '## Stop and get help' section; this one carries none.

The 38 values themselves are correct, complete and inside their boxes on both fixtures. The FAIL is that the delivered records and the delivered guide state, three times over, that the packet wrote nothing on the court's order page while it wrote five things there. production-field-map.json refuses 18 fields on packet page 4 (CC-DC-089 page 3) and gives every one of them the same reason: 'page 3 of this form is the court's order on the request and every field on it belongs to the court'. build-findings.json says 'Page 3 of CC-DC-089 is the court's order on the request. In the delivered bytes that page carries five writes from the same field map: the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box is TICKED, and Court's City/County, Case No., Petitioner/Plaintiff and Respondent/Defendant are all printed. I read them off the rendered page 4 and counted their ink. The same refusals array contradicts itself in place - its first page-4 entry refuses the CIRCUIT COURT box with the reason 'the packet states the other member of this select-one', which is the tick the blanket sentence says does not exist. This is the participant-facing consequence and it is why it is a FAIL rather than a note: the caption on a proposed order names the court that will sign it and the case it will be signed in, and the packet tells the person filing that nothing on that page is theirs to check. Repair is in the copy and the refusal basis, not in the geometry: the caption is correctly filled and should be described as filled.

Every selection the packet makes is defensible on its face, and half of them are hidden from the person who signs. The packet ticks four controls: (1) item 3's pardon ground, with the pardon date written beside it - disclosed in its own section of the guide, with the warning to check the date against the pardon document; (2) CC-DC-089's 'I request a waiver of the prepaid costs' - disclosed in one sentence; (3) the DISTRICT COURT OF MARYLAND caption box, on the petition and on both CC-DC-089 widgets, on the field map's basis 'the court of conviction held by this fixture is a District Court location'; and (4) item 1's 'I was arrested', on the basis 'the held case fact is an arrest rather than a summons or a citation'. Item 1 is the one that matters: the form prints '(Check one of the following boxes) On or about ___, I was [ ] arrested, [ ] served with a summons, [ ] or served with a citation', the packet answers that select-one from an inference (factId null, routeDetermined false), and the petition is affirmed under the penalties of perjury. Actionable repair: list all four in routeSelectionsMade and disclose selections 3 and 4 to the participant in the same terms the other two already get. Correctly NOT ticked: the other seven grounds of item 3, which the form makes a check-all-that-apply and which the packet carries as genuine participant elections with the form's own words beside each; and items 4 and 5, the transfer and appeal questions that decide the court.

PLACEMENT, which is the harder half here, is correct and was verified independently: CR-307's AcroForm field names are shifted by one against its printed labels, so the widget named 'Defendants DOB mmddyyyy' is in fact the caption's defendant-name box and the widget named 'MOTION TO SEAL CONVICTION FOR' is in fact the DOB box. FORMAT is the failure: CR-307 prints its DOB blank as 'Defendant's DOB (mm/dd/yyyy):' and CR-308 names the same widget 'Defendants DOB mmddyyyy', and the packet writes '1991-04-17' on both, in ISO-8601, on both the canonical and the boundary fixture. The packet demonstrably knows the rule — participant-instructions.md tells the participant to supply the conviction date 'in mm/dd/yyyy' for the blank it declines to write — and does not apply it to the value it does write. Nothing in production-field-map.json, reports/blanks.json, build-findings.json or either guide records a decision to deviate, so it is an undisclosed deviation from the official form's own printed instruction on a motion the participant signs.

The quantity FIX01 repaired is confirmed and is not what fails. All 11 requiredBeforeFiling strings from the packet-set manifest reach the delivered guides as exact substrings, tested here by literal substring match, 11/11, against 0 before the repair. What fails is that two of the strings published are addressed to the operator of the service and are now printed to the participant under the heading 'You must supply these before you file', introduced by the sentence 'These are the blanks on the forms themselves that this packet leaves for you'. (1) participant-instructions.md line 114 reads in full: 'No fee is expected, on the same analysis as the general sealing track: Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26) lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion. Confirm with the clerk and do not promise a refund.' 'Do not promise a refund' is an instruction to LegalEase about what it may tell a participant, printed to the participant as something they must supply. The same fee fact is rendered correctly participant-facing in filing-instructions.md, which drops that clause and says 'This packet states no fee amount. Ask the clerk.' — so the packet contains both the right rendering and the raw record string, in two guides, for the same fact. (2) Under 'Documents to gather', the guide introduces a block with 'On documentation of victim status in particular, the record says:' and then quotes 'Frame the question so a no carries no implication, and never ask the participant to produce proof.' That sentence is a questionnaire-design instruction to the builder, quoted to the participant as the record speaking to them, and it refers to them in the third person. The section's own framing does not cover either instance: it discloses only that 'Some of its entries record that nothing is required rather than asking you for something', which explains the bare 'none.' and 'none expected, because no fee is expected.' entries but says nothing about operator-directed text. The guide proves elsewhere that it knows how to make this disclosure, and makes it for the self-help stop conditions 80 lines earlier. This is DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE 'internal record text printed on a filing' — present, non-empty, in its section, verbatim from a controlling record, and therefore invisible to every counter — and it was introduced by the repair, because before it these strings were absent from participant copy altogether.

The record's fee rule for this route ends with an instruction about the packet itself: 'Whether the $125.00 filing fee and the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee apply is recorded below as an open question, SO THE PACKET MUST NOT STATE A PRICE.' Currency figures survive in BOTH delivered instruction documents, eight times: participant-instructions.md lines 51, 78 and 91 and filing-instructions.md lines 19, 41 and 56 each carry '$125.00' and '$100'. That leaves two assurances the delivered guide makes about itself false on their face. It says 'This packet does not state a price for this petition, and that is deliberate' in the same paragraph that prints $125.00; and, of the Circuit Court Filing Fees schedule, it says 'Its figure is deliberately not repeated here' when that schedule's figure is $125.00 and it is repeated twice within eight lines of that sentence and four times in the document. The builder plainly understood the rule as no currency figure reaching the participant -- it went to the trouble of naming the schedule by prefix and URL rather than by its title, because the title carries the amount -- and then did not apply the same rule to the body. Recorded in fairness: every figure is a verbatim quotation of the controlling record, nothing is invented, the packet asserts no price as due, the figures appear as the subject of a declared open question, and the substantive guidance is right -- ask the clerk before you pay, and the waiver papers NHJB-2311 and NHJB-2328 are named and prepared and delivered. The defect is the false self-description plus the leak, not a fabricated fee. The repair is small and does not require giving up verbatim fidelity: elide the two amounts where the record's fee rule is quoted and say that they are elided, or drop the two sentences that claim they are absent.

failedObligations.finding: This is the question this lane was asked to answer, and the answer is that the gap is real. The Colorado Judicial Department publishes JDF 491, 'Guide to Sealing Non-Conviction Records (simplified process)', at revision R: August 7, 2024 — the same revision date as both bound forms. Its step 2, headed 'File the Request — File these forms into your criminal case', names four forms with no branch and no condition between them: JDF 477 Motion, JDF 492 Order (just do §§ A-C), JDF 493 Notice (Just do §§ A-C), and JDF 478 Order (just do §§ A-C). Page 2 confirms it is one process, for cases ending in acquittal, a completed diversion agreement, a completed deferred judgment or a vacated conviction, under C.R.S. §§ 24-72-705 and 707 — the same statute and the same dispositions as this route. The packet delivers two of those four. JDF 492 and JDF 493 appear NOWHERE: not in the delivered packet, not in the packet-set manifest's components, not in the track registry entry, not in any file in the family directory (grepped), and not anywhere under STATES/CO in the master library, so they are a source-acquisition gap as well as a component gap. Nothing records the absence — there is no missing-component note, no open source item, no conditionDescription and no sentence in the participant guide telling a filer that the court's own guide names two more documents. The delivered guide instead states without qualification that 'This packet is two Colorado Judicial Department forms, filed together'. This lane read JDF 491 itself rather than a summary of it; its digest is 79dca4e720161b68ae74a8973392bbe22c05f565f704c609ec7cc7da0fcd3685 at STATES/CO/03_INSTRUCTIONS/CO__INSTRUCTIONS__JDF-491__guide-to-sealing-non-conviction-records__REV-2024-08-07__EN.pdf. This lane does not conclude that JDF 491 is right and the manifest wrong; it concludes that two committed sources disagree about what this route owes, that the disagreement is recorded nowhere, and that a route sells only what a record proves it delivers.

Two defects on the order the judge signs, both invisible to every counter because every value is present, non-empty, inside its declared write rect and equal to its expected value. FIRST, a value written into a field about something else. JDF-478 draws four separate fields in section 2c and each carries its own tooltip in the form's own metadata: '∆ Street Address' — "Enter the Defendant's street address.", '∆ City', '∆ State' and '∆ Zip'. The packet writes participant.street_address into '∆ Street Address' as the full concatenated value '412 Cherry Creek Way, Denver, CO 80202' and ALSO writes Denver, CO and 80202 into the three dedicated fields, so the delivered page 4 reads 'c) Mailing Address: 412 Cherry Creek Way, Denver, CO 80202 / City: Denver ST: CO Zip Code: 80202' and the city, state and ZIP are each printed twice on the proposed order. On the boundary fixture the duplication is a whole line long: the street field carries '1188 Upper Notch Crossing Road, Apartment 14B, Colorado Springs, Colorado 80921-2214' beside '∆ City' Colorado Springs and '∆ Zip' 80921-2214. The combined form is correct on JDF-477, whose field is captioned 'Current Mailing Address: (with city/state/zip)' and carries no tooltip — so the same fact is right on one form and wrong on the other, and the map's own label for the JDF-478 write is the printed caption 'Mailing Address' rather than the widget's declared purpose, which is how it read clean. This family's own municipal sibling writes street-only into the equivalent JDF-686 field with city, state and ZIP separate, so the correct behaviour exists in the same cohort. SECOND, a value that contradicts the field's own printed instruction. '∆ State' declares "Enter the state (use two letter abbreviation) in the Defendant's mailing address." and the boundary fixture writes 'Colorado'. It fits the 33.1 pt field and renders cleanly, so no geometry check sees it. Placement itself was verified for all 17 canonical and 16 boundary writes by reading the delivered pages with pdftotext and matching each value to the printed caption beside it, and every drawnText equals its expected value; the failure is which field the value went into and in what form, not where on the page it landed.

Four of the seven requiredBeforeFiling items in the controlling packet-set manifest reach the delivered guide neither verbatim nor in substance, and two of the four are substantive participant obligations rather than record boilerplate. Missing entirely, tested by literal substring match and then by keyword search of the whole delivered guide: (1) 'Obtain Colorado criminal-history report. Request a criminal-history report from CBI and attach it if the form requires it.' — the strings 'criminal-history' and 'criminal history' occur ZERO times in participant-instructions.md; the CBI appears only as an agency to list and notify, never as the source of a report the participant must obtain. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

failedObligations.finding: The route declares five dispositions and the packet delivers one, presenting the other four as belonging to no route. data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track il-seal-2yr, dispositions = ['supervision_successfully_completed', 'qualified_probation', 'conditional_discharge_completed_without_revocation', 'probation_completed_without_revocation', 'misdemeanor_conviction'], and its mechanism sentence reads 'a two-year sealing bucket effective June 1, 2026, covering successfully completed supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, and misdemeanor convictions'. Its own requiredBeforeFiling line asks the participant to check the answer to 'For each case, was the outcome supervision, qualified probation, conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, a misdemeanor conviction, or a felony conviction?' -- a multi-way question. The delivered Request page 5 prints all four two-year grounds: Section 16 (supervision, 2 years), Section 17 (misdemeanor conviction, 2 years), Section 18 (qualified probation / Cannabis Control Act Section 10 / Controlled Substances Act Section 410 / Meth Act Section 70 / Offender Initiative Program, 2 years) and Section 19.a (conditional discharge or probation completed without revocation, 2 years). The packet ticks Section 17 only. production-field-map.json refuses Section 16, Section 18 and Section 19.a with the string 'A participant election or financial fact not determined by this packet route' and routeDetermined: false. That reason is untrue of this route: those three printed grounds ARE this route's other declared dispositions. participant-instructions.md never mentions Section 16, Section 18 or Section 19.a. It names only Section 17 and a negative election of Section 15. A participant on this track whose disposition is supervision, qualified probation, or unrevoked conditional discharge or probation -- four of the track's five dispositions -- is handed a petition that states the wrong ground and is told nothing about which box states theirs, on a document they verify under 735 ILCS 5/1-109. failedObligations.finding: THE BRIEF ASKED WHICH OF THE TWO THIS IS. IT IS BOTH, AND THE OBLIGATION MEASURES WHAT IS PRESENT RATHER THAN WHAT WAS DISCLOSED, SO IT FAILS. What is delivered: attachments 4, 5 and 6 of in_conviction_serious_felony-set - the Appearance, Form ACR and the Confidential Information Form - and nothing else. What the three bound routes require and nobody renders: ten components. I verified the builder's claim independently rather than taking it, by searching the packetComponents of all 346 families in MASTER_QUEUE for the three track ids; the only components any family declares for in_conviction_serious_felony, in_collateral_action or in_supplemental_order are the three attachments this family delivers. So no family in the queue builds the serious-felony petition, its proposed order, its attachment-3 or its instructions component, and neither of the other two routes has a single component declared anywhere. A participant on any of these three routes cannot file with this packet: it contains no petition and no proposed order, and an Appearance and a notice of exclusion filed alone commence nothing. THE DISCLOSURE IS EXEMPLARY AND I RECORD IT IN FULL. participant-instructions.md opens 'What is in this packet, and what is not', its second heading is 'Read this first: these three forms are not the filing', and it says in terms 'The petition itself is not in this packet, and neither is the proposed order. If you file only these three sheets, you have not asked the court for anything', and then that neither of the other two routes' own filings is built here either. filing-instructions.md carries a section headed 'What this packet does NOT contain', and production-field-map.json lists all ten under componentsOfThisFamilysOwnRoutesThatNothingBuilds. That disclosure is why this is a queue scope decision - widen this family or open two more - rather than a build error, and the build lane says so itself. ONE MORE THING I MEASURED THAT BEARS ON THE SCOPE DECISION: three sibling Indiana families - in-conviction-felony-set, in-conviction-misd-set and in-conviction-d6-set - each deliver a COMPLETE ten-page packet whose pages 7-10 are these very same three documents, and they deliver them BLANK. I confirmed it by hashing the extracted text of every page of each: their page 8 is textually identical to this family's page 2, and their pages 7, 9 and 10 are the same three documents with 'STATE OF INDIANA ____________' and 'PETITIONER'S NAME: ______' unfilled. So the fill this family maps is genuinely owed work that nothing else does; it is simply attached to routes whose filings nobody builds.

No signature, signature date or court-only field carries a VALUE - both signature rules on the Appearance, the signature rule on Form ACR, all three cause-number lines and the full Social Security number box are empty on the delivered pages, and I confirmed each. THE FAILURE IS THAT FOUR CERTIFICATE-OF-SERVICE CONTROLS CARRY INK THIS BUILD DREW. A certificate of service asserts that service has happened; this family's own approval-request calls a ticked one 'the single worst defect this packet could carry' and asks a reviewer to confirm both boxes are empty on each of the two documents. They are not empty. On packet page 2 (the Appearance's certificate of service) and packet page 3 (Form ACR's), each of the four alternatives' checkbox widgets is flattened as an appearance whose entire content is '0.5 0.5 17 17 re s' - a stroked rectangle - and that rectangle is stamped onto the page. Proved against the pinned source, not inferred: rendering source page 2 and delivered page 2 at 200 dpi and differencing them gives 554 added dark pixels and zero removed, in exactly two hollow squares of 277 pixels at x 110.2-121.7pt, on a page that carries no value write at all; the crop shows the form's own checkbox with a second, smaller square drawn inside it. reports/actual-writes.json publishes refusedFieldsWithInk: [] for both fixtures and that is false as delivered.

EIGHT FLATTENED WIDGET APPEARANCES PER FIXTURE STAMP A RECTANGLE THE FORM DOES NOT PRINT ONTO THE DELIVERED PAGE. This is the same defect mo-art-xiv-marijuana-set was failed and repaired for - pdf-lib's default appearance provider reading /MK /BC for a widget with no usable /AP /N, with flatten then stamping the invention - and this factory's own scan-synthesized-widget-borders.mjs names the mechanism precisely. Measured, not inferred. (1) From the bytes: of 46 flattened appearance XObjects per fixture, 20 carry show-text, 18 are empty and 8 contain a path-paint operator and no text at all; their entire decompressed content is '0.5 0.5 9.599 11.8762 re s' at four page-1 checkboxes and '0.5 0.5 17 17 re s' at two page-2 and two page-3 checkboxes. Identical in canonical and boundary. (2) From the pixels, against the pinned source: differencing 200-dpi renders of source page 2 against delivered page 2 gives 554 added dark pixels and 0 removed, in exactly two hollow 277-pixel squares - and delivered page 2 carries no value write, so those pixels are the whole of what this build added to it. Page 3 gives the same two. Cropping the page-1 'I will accept service at the above email address' box shows the shape: the source draws the form's own checkbox; the delivered page draws that box AND a second, offset square inside it. Every other limb of this obligation is clean and I record it: no run is wider than its own box in either fixture (measured with Helvetica advance widths, including the boundary fixture's 39-character hyphenated name and 60-character email, which the finalizer shrinks to 8pt and 7.5pt and which fit), every one of the 13 ink runs is inside its own widget rect and appearance BBox, and no two runs overlap. FIX80's cohort does not list this family only because the scan predates its build; five of its Indiana siblings ARE in that cohort, with 659 exposed widgets between them.

39 of the 40 stop conditions the three bound routes declare are carried VERBATIM, and I checked each one string by string against IN.memo.json rather than reading a count: in_conviction_serious_felony 13 of 13, in_supplemental_order 13 of 13, in_collateral_action 13 of 14. THE ONE THAT IS MISSING IS THE ONLY ONE UNIQUE TO ITS ROUTE: 'The court finds the collateral action does not relate to the expunged matter.' It is absent from participant-instructions.md, absent from filing-instructions.md and absent from all four delivered pages - I searched for it verbatim and for 'does not relate' and 'collateral action does not relate' in every delivered byte, and there is no occurrence and no paraphrase. The guide's stop list under 'When this is not a do-it-yourself matter' prints exactly the thirteen the serious-felony track declares, introduced as 'The record names these as the points where the filing these forms accompany stops being a self-help matter' - but three routes are bound to this family and the guide gives each of them its own filing, fee, notice and service section, so a participant on the collateral-action route reads a stop list from which their own route's distinctive condition has been dropped. Narrow, provable and worth naming so a repair carries it: the other thirty-nine need no work. (The guide claims no count, so this is a shortfall against the record rather than a false statement about itself.)

failedObligations.finding: No protected field carries ink - protectedWrites is a measured zero and EXP106 pages 2 and 3 and EXP104 page 2 are pixel-identical to their pinned sources - but the delivered participant copy tells the participant that the court's own fields are theirs. participant-instructions.md, in the section whose whole subject is which boxes are already marked, says: 'This packet marks 2 boxes for you and no others. They are listed below. Every other box on every form in this packet is empty, and every one of them is yours to decide.' That is false of 40 empty boxes on the delivered pages, all of which production-field-map.json itself classifies PROTECTED_FIELD. 36 of them are on EXP106, the proposed order: the Appearances boxes on page 1, the 'has / has not been given' service finding, the 'is / is not clear and convincing evidence' finding and the 'is / is not a nexus' finding on page 2, the granted and denied boxes on page 2, the whole agency-application checklist on page 2, and on page 3 item 5's box together with its two inner branches (whether the order seals the record under Minn. Stat. § 152.18 or finds a crime-victim nexus), item 6 and item 8. The other 4 are the hearing-notice boxes at the top of EXP102 page 1, which the same guide contradicts itself about two sections later by listing them under 'The court fills these in after you file'. Nothing anywhere in either delivered guide tells the participant that EXP106's boxes belong to the judge: the only sentence about EXP106's completion is 'EXP106 is signed by the judge, not by you', which is about the signature, and the guide separately instructs the participant to write the Judicial District onto EXP106's caption - so the participant is told to write on this form and told every empty box on it is theirs to decide. A participant who follows the guide can mark the judge's findings, the grant-or-deny box and the sealing branch on a proposed order before filing it. Every counter reads zero with this present.

rasterRule: **A missing Chromium is not a source blocker and it is not a legal blocker.** ENV-RAS01 established that a Codex container cannot resolve or fetch one -- the Playwright CDN answers HTTP 403 from inside it. That is an environment fact about the container, not a fact about the packet, and classifying it as BLOCKED_SOURCE would put a packet defect on a record that has none.

**And if your container DOES resolve a browser, that changes nothing about whose raster counts.** Two lanes have now reported building a page image locally, and they were right to discard it: a local render is not a receipt. Only the central gate below produces one, bound to the exact bytes the queue pinned and published as an artifact this factory can admit. Use a local render to measure something if it helps you, delete it, and still return `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` with `visualDefects` untouched.
Finish every nonvisual obligation. Record the exact SHA-256 of the canonical and boundary PDFs you produced. Return the family `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING`.

Put that in `rasterState`. `status` is the row's own outcome and takes exactly `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`: a repair that finished is `COMPLETED` even though nobody has rastered it, because `status` records whether YOU finished, not whether a page was looked at. The post-repair reader in `generate.mjs` takes only rows whose `status` is `COMPLETED`, so a finished repair filed as `BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` leaves its family sitting in FAIL.

`countersBefore` and `countersAfter` hold exactly the nine counters and nothing else -- that reader requires every value to be numerically zero, so a prose key alongside them (`measuredBy`, a caveat, even a boolean `allNineZero`) makes the whole object read as non-zero. Put the prose in siblings and keep every word of it.

`BUILT_RASTER_PENDING` is a factory workflow state and not a launch verdict. It zeroes nothing and waives nothing: visualDefects stays whatever it is, because it records that nobody has looked, not that there is nothing to see. **No packet becomes PASS_COMPLETE without RASTER_PASS.**

The render happens in `.github/workflows/rcap-packet-raster-acceptance-batch.yml` on a browser-equipped runner, against the exact bytes your hashes pin. RASTER_PASS sends the family to independent verification; RASTER_FAIL sends it to FIX.
Page rasters go through `scripts/raster/pdf-page-raster.mjs`. It discovers its own browser and calibrates the page-to-pixel mapping against both the paper bounds and stamped marks.
NEVER `pdftoppm`. NEVER `apt-get`. NEVER `playwright install`. The environment refuses package installation and a Poppler fallback is not a fallback, it is a different measurement.
The preflight now gates on the rasterizer resolving a browser it can execute, so a lane that cannot raster learns before it builds rather than after.

failedObligations.finding: Two committed controlling records make obtaining a CORI a required-before-filing act and the delivered guide never discloses it. (1) data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json, packetSet ma-expunge-k-set, participantActionRequired[0]: kind obtain_document, requirement required, requiredBeforeFiling true, obtainedFrom 'Massachusetts Department of Criminal Justice Information Services', description 'Obtain Your own CORI from the Department of Criminal Justice Information Services. Request your personal CORI from DCJIS.' The same string is the first entry of that packetSet's requiredBeforeFiling array. (2) data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track ma-expunge-k, packetSet.participantActionRequired[0] carries the identical item. participantActionRequired[1] is the paired confirm_answer item, 'Check your answer to "What is the docket number?" against Your own CORI ... and correct the packet if they disagree', also requiredBeforeFiling true. WHAT THE DELIVERED GUIDE ACTUALLY SAYS: I read participant-instructions.md end to end and grepped it. It contains three references to a CORI and all three are as an OPTIONAL ALTERNATIVE SOURCE to copy from, never as a document to obtain — line 64 'Write in the docket number and the charges from your own court papers or your CORI', line 85 'copied from your own court papers or from your CORI', line 87 'listed from your own court papers or CORI'. There is no step directing the participant to obtain it, no 'documents you must obtain first' section anywhere in the guide, and the only occurrence of 'Department of Criminal Justice Information' (line 7) is inside a quotation from the court's instruction sheet about which agencies must DESTROY records on expungement — the opposite role. DCJIS is never named. A participant who follows the guide's own numbered eight-step list and holds their court papers never obtains a CORI at all, and never performs the confirm_answer cross-check, because neither is stated. THE FAMILY'S OWN CLAIM AND WHY IT READS CLEAN: reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json asserts everyRequiredBeforeFilingItemIsDisclosed true with disclosedIn participant-instructions.md, but its requiredBeforeFiling array holds 16 entries and every one of them is a FORM BLANK on the petition face; the controlling records' seven participant-action strings are outside its scope, so the assertion is true of a narrower set than its name claims. This is the same defect shape and the same standard on which this lane failed co_petition_seal_arrest-set on 20260909b, where the record's obtain_document item (the CBI criminal-history report) was likewise absent from the guide while the guide mentioned the agency in a different role.

Fresh downloads of all six individual forms from the official UJS Expungement Forms page match four receipt pins exactly and contradict two. UJS-232 is now c76ac268.../177827 bytes rather than 308ed5e4.../166791 bytes, with a changed layout despite the same 12/2020 footer. UJS-394 is now 5cbdcdf2.../188446 bytes, Rev. 07/2026, while packet page 11 and the receipt retain d6f2dab3.../92135 bytes, Rev. 08/2024. The family does not bind the current official six-form set.
